message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the **presence of a mane in adult males**. The allele that codes for mane development is dominant over the allele that results in a maneless phenotype. In other words, if a male lion inherits just one copy of the mane allele (from either parent), he will develop a full mane; only when both copies are the recessive “maneless” allele will the lion grow without a mane. This dominant inheritance pattern is why most male lions in the wild have prominent manes, while females and some males (especially younger ones) do not.
